2. The petitioners as plaintiffs instituted the suit for partition being Title Suit No. 23 of 2013 in the Court of the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Manikganj Sadar, Manikganj. The defendants-opposite parties contested the suit. Upon hearing the parties and considering the evidence on record the learned Senior Assistant Judge decreed the suit in preliminary form. Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and decree of the said Court, defendants preferred appeal which was dismissed. Then they filed a Revisional application to the High Court Division which was pleased to discharge the Rule. Then the defendants preferred leave to Appeal No. 2456 of 2013 which was also dismissed by the Appellate Division on 22-8-2016. The opposite party Nos. 1-4 filed an application under Order 1, Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 for adding as parties while the suit is pending for drawing final decree. Upon hearing, learned Assistant Judge, Manikganj rejected the application. On revision learned District Judge Manikganj set-aside the said Order and allowed the petition for addition of party and being aggrieved by dissatisfied with the petitioners filed an application for leave to Revision under section 115(4) of the CPC and obtained the Rule. 

 4. Mr Asif Parvez, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the opposite party Nos. 1-4 are not necessary party. While the Title Suit No. 23 of 2003 is pending for drawing final decree, the application for adding as defendants is nothing but to prolong the litigation. He also submitted that learned Senior Assistant Judge after perusing the materials on record rightly rejected the petition for addition of party but unfortunately, learned District Judge most illegally allowed the Revisional application and, as such, committed an error of law occasioning failure of justice, therefore, the aforesaid Judgment and Order of the learned District Judge is liable to be set-aside. He also submitted that as the preliminary decree was upheld up to the Appellate Division, therefore, the opposite parties have no right to be impleaded as defendants. He has also submitted that the opposite party Nos. 1-4 have got no title and interest in the suit land as their predecessor transferred the entire his land. From judicial pronouncements, it is now settled that the person whose presence is required under the law and whose absence no effective decision can be given, are necessary parties.  5. It appears from the record, learned Senior Assistant Judge rejected the petition for added as defendant stating that there is no reason to be added as defendant at the stage when preliminary decree is yet to be made final. The learned District Judge set-aside the Order holding the view- 

 6. In the case of Alekjan Bewa and others vs Arefa Bewa, 7 ADC (2010) 593 it was held that a partition suit remains pending after passing of the preliminary decree until decree is made final. So, if any co-sharer makes any prayer for any share after passing of the preliminary decree, his prayer for allotment of share may be considered and share may be given from the remaining joint property without disturbing the share of the plaintiff or shares of the other defendants who got shares. 

 7. A partition suit does not come to an end with the passing of preliminary decree and continues till the final decree is passed and an application can be made for amendment of the plaint if an event changing the shares of the parties occurs or parties may be added after preliminary decree and their rights adjusted in the final decree. This view finds support from the decisions of the cases of Venkata vs Balakrishna, AIR 7947 Mad 47 and Jadu vs Parmeswar, AIR 1940 PC 11. I am of the view that in order to avoid multiplicity of suits the opposite party Nos. 1-4 should have given an opportunity to be added as party. Admittedly they did not prefer any appeal. If the trial Court finds that the opposite party Nos. 1-4 have share in the suit land, they will get their due saham without disturbing the preliminary decree.
